newsitem.title: ITALY: Blair family heads for poolside holiday in Tuscany.
newsitem.headline: Blair family heads for poolside holiday in Tuscany.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair and his family arrived in sunny Italy on Saturday for two weeks of poolside relaxation at a villa in the Tuscan countryside.

Blair, looking relaxed and happy to be on holiday, arrived with his wife Cherie and three children at Bologna Airport, where they were greeted by Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and his wife, Flavia.

While the wives and children took a sight-seeing tour of the mediaeval city, which is built mainly of red brick and lined with elegant colonnades, Blair and Prodi met for just under an hour of informal talks.
Blair told a news conference later that he was happy to be in Italy and that his holidays were finally about to begin.

"I am delighted...that this will be my last press conference for the next couple of weeks," said Blair, who with his family left later for Tuscany where they were to stay at a villa owned by British junior minister Geoffrey Robinson.
The white neoclassical villa a few kilometres from the mediaeval hilltown of San Gimignano is surrounded by tall cypress trees, covered with vineyards and equipped with a swimming pool.

Blair and his family also spent their holidays there last summer. The region has been dubbed "Chianti-shire" by the British press after the area's famous flasked red wine and its large English expatriate community.
At the news conference, Blair and Prodi said their talks were "good and frank" and said strong bilateral ties would be beneficial to both countries, as well as to Europe.
Later, the Labour leader and Prodi, who heads a centre-left coalition, walked down Bologna's cobblestoned streets to the city hall, where Blair signed the town register.
They then visited a memorial site in a nearby square for victims of bomb attacks in Bologna over the past two decades.

At the site, Blair exchanged a few words with Britons Harry and Shirley Mitchell, whose daughter Catherine was killed aged 21 in a bomb attack here in which a total of 85 people died and 200 were injured exactly 17 years ago.
